## Import Dataset

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
student_risk <- read_csv("student_dropout_risk_2026.csv")
is.tibble(student_risk)

View(student_risk)
```

## EDA

Converting 0/1 variables to Yes/No variables and forcing all categorical variables to be factors, including imposing ordering on family income level.

```{r}
student_risk <- student_risk |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        first_generation,
        tuition_up_to_date,
        disability_status,
        scholarship_holder,
        part_time_job,
        international_student,
        dropout
      ),
      ~ factor(.x,
               levels = c(0, 1),
               labels = c("No", "Yes"))
    ),
    
    across(
      c(gender, nationality, course_type, study_mode),
      as.factor
    ),
    
    family_income_level = factor(
      family_income_level,
      levels = c("Low", "Middle", "High"),
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )
saveRDS(student_risk, "student_risk.rds")
```

### Categorical Tables and Summaries

Determine how many variables have missing values. There are not any missing values in this data set.

```{r}
colSums(is.na(student_risk))
```

View the number of responses for each level of the categorical variables.

```{r}
lapply(
  student_risk |>  select(where(is.factor)),
  table
)
```

Create two and three way tables to examine relationships in the data.

```{r}
#examine gender and nationality
table(student_risk$gender, student_risk$nationality)

#examine scholarship status and family income level
prop.table(table(student_risk$family_income_level, student_risk$scholarship_holder))

#examine scholarship status, family income, and gender
prop.table(
  table(student_risk$family_income_level, student_risk$scholarship_holder, student_risk$gender))

#examine course of study and dropout
prop.table(
  table(student_risk$course_type, student_risk$dropout)
)

#examine study mode and dropout
prop.table(
  table(student_risk$study_mode, student_risk$dropout))

#examine dropout by gender
prop.table(table(student_risk$gender))

#examine study course of study, gender and dropout
prop.table(
  table(student_risk$course_type, student_risk$dropout, student_risk$gender)
)

#examine first generation student and dropout
prop.table(
  table(student_risk$first_generation, student_risk$dropout)
)
```

#### Visualizations

```{r}
#create visualizations to examine relationship between nationality and gender
ggplot(student_risk,
       aes(x = nationality, fill = gender)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", width=0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Proportion of Gender Within Nationalities",
    y = "Proportion",
    x = "Nationality",
    fill= "Gender"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

#create visualization to examine relationship between scholarship status, family income, and gender
ggplot(student_risk,
       aes(x = family_income_level,
           fill = scholarship_holder)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  facet_wrap(~ gender) +
  labs(
    title = "Scholarship Status by Income and Gender",
    x = "Family Income Level",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Scholarship Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

#create visualization to examine dropout rate by course type using counts
ggplot(student_risk,
       aes(x = course_type,
           fill = dropout)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Dropout Rate by Course Type",
    x = "Course Type",
    y = "Count",
    fill = 'Dropout Status'
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

#create visualization to examine dropout rate by course type using proportions
ggplot(student_risk,
       aes(x = course_type,
           fill = dropout)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    title = "Dropout Rate by Course Type",
    x = "Course Type",
    y = "Proportion", 
    fill = 'Dropout Status'
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )+ coord_flip()

#Heatmap for first generation and dropout status
student_risk |>
  count(first_generation, dropout) |>
  ggplot(aes(first_generation, dropout, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    x = "First-Generation Status",
    y = "Dropout Status",
    fill = "Count of Students",
    title = "Relationship Between First-Generation Status and Dropout Risk"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


#Heatmap for first generation and dropout status using proportions
student_risk |>
  count(first_generation, dropout) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(first_generation, dropout, fill = prop)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 0.1)),
            color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    x = "First-Generation Status",
    y = "Dropout Status",
    fill = "Percent of Students",
    title = "Relationship Between First-Generation Status and Dropout Risk"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

### Numerical Summaries

Find the mean, standard deviation, median, minimum and maximum values for each numerical variable.

```{r}
#Create numerical summaries for all numerical variables except person_id and format in a table
table_student_risk <- student_risk |> 
  select(-person_id) |> 
  summarize(across(where(is.numeric),
    list(
    Mean= \(x) mean(x,na.rm=TRUE), 
    std= \(x) sd(x, na.rm=TRUE),
    Median= \(x) median(x,na.rm=TRUE),
    Min = \(x) min(x, na.rm=TRUE),
    Max = \(x) max(x, na.rm=TRUE)), .names='{.col}_{.fn}') ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = c("Variable", "Statistic"),
    names_sep = "_(?=[^_]+$)"
  )


#create summaries of weekly work hours by family income
table_work_hours <- student_risk |>
  group_by(family_income_level) |>
  summarize(
    across(
      weekly_work_hours,
      list(
        Mean   = \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
        SD     = \(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
        Median = \(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
        Min    = \(x) min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
        Max    = \(x) max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    ),
   .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("weekly_work_hours"),
    names_to = c("Variable", "Statistic"),
    names_sep = "_(?=[^_]+$)"
  )

table_work_hours


#create summaries of attendance rate by dropout status
table_attendance <- student_risk |>
  group_by(dropout) |>
  summarize(
    across(
      attendance_rate,
      list(
        Mean   = \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
        SD     = \(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
        Median = \(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
        Min    = \(x) min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
        Max    = \(x) max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("attendance_rate"),
    names_to = c("Variable", "Statistic"),
    names_sep = "_(?=[^_]+$)"
  )

table_attendance
```

#### Visualizations

```{r}
#create histogram of age
student_risk |> 
  ggplot(aes(age))+geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, color='blue', fill='red')+
  labs(x = "Age",
       y = "Count",
       title = "Histogram of Age of Students")+
  theme_minimal()

#create histogram of weekly work hours by family income level
student_risk |>
  ggplot(aes(x = weekly_work_hours)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 1,
    fill = "blue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ family_income_level) +
  labs(
    x = "Weekly Work Hours",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Weekly Work Hours by Family Income Level"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

#the histogram is difficult to interpret because of the large number of students that don't work.  Use a boxplot instead.
student_risk |>
  ggplot(aes(x = family_income_level, y = weekly_work_hours)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill='orange') +
  facet_wrap(~dropout)+
  labs(
    x = "Family Income Level",
    y = "Hours Worked Weekly",
    title = "Weekly Work Hours by Family Income Level",
    subtitle = "By Dropout Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

#Create histogram for admission grade by first generation student status
student_risk |>
  ggplot(aes(x = admission_grade)) +
  geom_histogram(
    fill = "red",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ first_generation) +
  labs(
    x = "Admission Grade",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Admission Grade by First Generation Student Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


#compare distributions of attendance rate by dropout status
student_risk |>
  ggplot(aes(x = attendance_rate, fill=dropout)) +
  geom_density(alpha=0.2) +
  labs(
    x = "Attendance Rate",
    y = "Density",
    title = "Attendance Rate by Dropout Status",
    fill="Dropout"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

#create a violin plot
ggplot(student_risk,
       aes(x = dropout,
           y = attendance_rate,
           fill=dropout)) +
  geom_violin() +
  labs(
    x = "Dropout Status",
    y = "Attendance Rate",
    title = "Attendance Rate by Dropout Status",
    fill="Dropout Status"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal()


#create scatterplot examining weekly work hours and attendance rate
student_risk |>
  ggplot(aes(x = weekly_work_hours, y=attendance_rate)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(
    x = "Weekly Hours Worked",
    y = "Attendance Rate",
    title = "Weekly Hours Worked and Attendance Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


```
